The [preview deck](preview.html) is built by this site.
This page is the source behind it.
A tab arriving on an arrow press is not something a page of prose can show, so open the deck alongside this one.

## A tabset

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### First

The first tab.

### Second

The second, reached with the next arrow press.

:::
```

The arrow keys step through the tabs without leaving the keyboard.
The first press shows the first tab, and each later press brings the next tab.

## Opening on a given tab

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset .no-tabset-fragments tab-active="1"}

### One

### Two

:::
```

The index counts from zero, so `1` is the second tab and the slide arrives with `Two` open.
An index the tabset does not have falls back to the first tab.
The attribute is emitted as `data-tab-active` in the HTML.
It only applies to a tabset marked `.no-tabset-fragments`, because a tabset that steps always opens on its first tab.
The `.active` class on a tab heading is ignored in the same way.

## Fragments inside a tab

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### With reveals

- [First point.]{.fragment}
- [Second point.]{.fragment}

### Plain

:::
```

The points belong to their tab, so they arrive after that tab and before the next one.
A fragment in a later tab is never shown before its tab is.

## Several tabsets on one slide

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### A

### B

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### X

### Y

:::
```

They are navigated one after another rather than in parallel.
In a PDF export each tabset shows the tab of its own step on every page.

## Opting a tabset out of the stepping

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset .no-tabset-fragments}

### One

### Two

:::
```

The tabset is then left to Quarto: the tabs are clicked, the arrow keys skip it, and a PDF export prints it on one page showing the first tab.

## Printing

Under Quarto's default, `pdf-separate-fragments: true`, a PDF export has one page per step, and each page shows the tab of its step.
With `pdf-separate-fragments: false`, each tab is placed on its own page, and the page numbers read `N.1`, `N.2` and so on.

Opt a slide out where that is not wanted:

```markdown
## A slide {tabset-skip-pdf-clone="true"}
```

Its tabset then stays on one page, showing the first tab alone.
The attribute has no effect under `pdf-separate-fragments: true`, which gives every step its own page anyway.

The repository ships a short, standalone starting point you can copy: [`example.qmd`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-tabset/blob/main/example.qmd).
